newsitem.title: UK: London gold may try lower, palladium ponders.
newsitem.headline: London gold may try lower, palladium ponders.

text.p: Precious metal markets could be in for a testing time on Thursday ahead of the Comex option expiry at the end of the week and the likelihood that Russia will begin exporting platinum group metals (PGMs) this month, dealers said.
"I'm not viciously bearish (for gold). I think we have seen the lows and $347/$348 should hold. But even if it doesn't there is good support at $341," one dealer said.
The other focus for dealers was palladium and the confirmation from a senior Almaz official exports could begin later this month.
"It's all down to how the Russians manage this situation. If they try to get three months lost revenue at once, then that is a bit bearish," one PGM dealer said.
Gold fixed barely changed at $351.45 per ounce just five cents up on Wednesday and compared with a close of $352.40/$352.90.
New York on Wednesday and the Far East markets earlier today were generally lower as sentiment in gold edged towards bearish, although there was late short covering in Hong Kong.
Dealers said physical interest in gold was still high and that probably the price should hold over $350.00 today.
Palladium fixed lower at $150.50 down a dollar versus its Wednesday afternoon fixing but $5.00 under its close. By 1045 GMT it had rallied to $152.00/$153.00.
"It's going to get whipped about a bit until the Russia situation is clearer," a dealer said.

Russia, the largest exporter of palladium, has not shipped metal this year due to internal administrative problems and has yet to finalise its 1997 supply contract with Japan, the world's biggest user of the metal.
Dealers and market analysts said they had not heard of any contracts between Russia and Japanese trading houses.
Exports this month or next would almost certainly be on a spot basis into the dealer market, they said.

"The Japanese trade houses would be able to buy spot metal if they need it, but it is impossible to know the volumes (likely to be involved)," a market analyst said, adding that the palladium market was less tight now than it was last month.
But a palladium dealer warned that the first time anyone in the market had an offer from Almaz, heavy selling was certain.
Palladium's sister metal platinum was relatively unmoved and down just 40 cents at $381.00/$382.00 and silver was acent lower at $5.23/$5.24. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
